content:
OVERVIEW
- Large integrated health system (hospital + outpatient) evaluating Redwood for PHI-adjacent GenAI workloads.
- Two tracks running in parallel:
  1) App/innovation team driving pilot (summarization + patient support)
  2) IT Security / GRC driving requirements (auditability, retention/residency, identity)

KEY CONTACTS / ORG MAP (as understood)
- Innovation/App team: Director of Clinical Apps (champion), 2 staff engineers, 1 data science lead.
- IT Security: Security Architect (primary), GRC Manager (questionnaires), IAM lead (SSO/SAML).
- Procurement: not engaged yet; they asked to involve after security sign-off.

WHAT THEY’RE BUILDING / USE CASES
- Clinical summarization: generate visit summaries from clinician notes + structured chart context; emphasis on provenance and “no surprises” outputs.
- Patient support assistant: triage FAQs and draft responses (human-in-the-loop). They want strict PII/PHI boundaries; prefer “PHI-adjacent” first phase using de-identified text.
- Coding assistance: batch workflows (lower latency sensitivity) for internal revenue-cycle teams; cost sensitivity is higher here.

CURRENT STACK / OPTIONS THEY’RE COMPARING
- Shortlist includes: Azure OpenAI (already has some Microsoft footprint), AWS Bedrock (security comfort), and self-hosted vLLM in their VPC.
- Key comment from Security Architect: “We can’t be the team that owns GPU clusters again.” They want a managed option with strong controls.

DEPLOYMENT / DATA REQUIREMENTS (HIGH CONFIDENCE)
- Must run in customer-controlled network boundary (VPC) for initial pilot; on-prem option discussed but not required for phase 1.
- Data residency: US-only processing and storage. They asked specifically whether logs/telemetry can be region-locked.
- Retention: want ability to set/request retention windows for request/response payloads; default should be minimal. They asked about separate retention for audit logs vs application logs.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS + at-rest encryption; preference for customer-managed keys (KMS) for sensitive workloads.
- Audit logs: required for admin actions and access; they asked about export to their SIEM and what fields exist (who/what/when, model/version, policy changes).
- Identity: SSO/SAML required; asked about SCIM and role-based access (RBAC) for console access.

PILOT SCOPE (LATEST)
- Pilot focus: de-identified clinical note summarization + limited patient support draft responses.
- Dataset constraints: cannot share raw PHI outside approved boundary; they will provide de-identified sample set + acceptance criteria.
- Success criteria drafted on 5/14 call:
  - Latency: interactive summarization <2.5s p50 / <6s p95 for target prompt sizes (tbd after we see token distribution).
  - Throughput: initial low volume, but must demonstrate scaling path for peak clinic hours.
  - Auditability: confirm audit log export pattern + admin activity visibility.
  - Security: complete baseline questionnaire + provide evidence pack items under NDA.

COMMERCIAL / PACKAGING NOTES
- Strong preference for a time-boxed pilot with defined credits. They asked for guardrails on unit costs and what drives pricing (tokens, throughput, reserved capacity).
- Likely landing spot is Dedicated-in-VPC vs Private (full control plane) depending on how their security team interprets “managed control plane” and telemetry boundaries.

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2025-05-14: POC scoping call (Fireflies) with app team + IT security present. Agreed on de-identified dataset first; identified evidence pack needs.
- 2025-05-20 to 2025-06-03: Async Qs from Security on retention/residency wording and audit log coverage; asked for standardized answers (PMM/Security reviewing claims).
- 2025-06-11: Pilot closeout/decision call (Fireflies) — confirmed Dedicated vs Private still open; security gaps list captured; plan is to re-scope pilot around VPC + evidence delivery.

OPEN QUESTIONS (NEED FOLLOW-UP)
- Confirm if they require a BAA and at what stage it’s needed (pilot vs procurement). They used “HIPAA” language; we should keep wording precise and route to Legal/Security.
- Confirm whether they want request/response payload logging disabled by default (and what they consider acceptable for debugging).
- Confirm identity requirements: SAML only vs SAML+SCIM provisioning.

RISKS / WATCH-OUTS
- Messaging sensitivity: Security pushed back on “HIPAA-ready” phrasing; keep to verifiable controls (VPC, KMS, audit logs, retention options, SOC 2 process).
- Multi-stakeholder alignment: innovation team is moving faster than GRC; if we don’t respond quickly on evidence + questionnaire, momentum will stall.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS (INTERNAL)
- SE (Fatima) to send a pilot plan one-pager with explicit data boundaries, proposed architecture (VPC), and how we handle logging/retention.
- Security (Naomi/Daniel) to provide evidence pack index + process for SOC 2 report request under NDA; include audit log sample fields if approved.
- AE (Priyom) to schedule 45-min joint session: IT Security + App team + Redwood SE to finalize (a) deployment mode recommendation, (b) pilot timeline, (c) procurement path.

NOTES / QUOTES
- “We need auditability like a real enterprise system — who changed what, and where does it export.”
- “We can’t ship anything that looks like it stores PHI by default; retention controls need to be explicit.”
